content: The International Development and Education System (IDES) has established a coordinated global leadership initiative to empower countries in preventing human deaths caused by rabies. The tools, knowledge, and technologies required to eliminate rabies already exist, but countries need actionable plans, resource mobilization strategies, and political commitment to implement them effectively. The United Against Rabies collaboration provides a structured global strategy, harmonized guidance, and training to support countries in achieving rabies elimination. This collaboration leverages collective strengths to advocate for prioritizing rabies prevention, engage stakeholders in the global fight, and build the capacity needed to create an environment where countries can succeed. Rabies elimination is no longer an unattainable dream but a realistic goal supported by a unified global strategy. By combining resources and expertise, the collaboration empowers countries to save lives from this preventable yet devastating disease. The vision of Zero by 30 aims to eliminate human deaths from dog-mediated rabies by 2030. The global strategic plan offers a harmonized framework that countries can adapt and implement to create national and regional rabies elimination plans. These plans focus on building capacity, integrating rabies control with other health initiatives, and strengthening health systems to reach underserved populations. The collaboration engages stakeholders across sectors, unites public and private development partners, and catalyzes communities and nations to take ownership of their rabies elimination efforts. National and regional elimination plans enhance preparedness, surveillance, and resource mobilization. By fostering collaboration across ministries and improving national capacity, these plans promote the inclusion of dog bite treatments in health systems, increase access to vaccines for both humans and animals, and adopt a One Health approach. This integrated strategy maximizes resources and impact, helping countries achieve their Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) while building a healthier future. The United Against Rabies collaboration supports these efforts by raising awareness, advocating for prioritization, and promoting prevention strategies. For the first time, a unified global effort is underway, with synergy and structure, to coordinate interventions and maximize the impact of investments in rabies elimination. Rabies is a preventable disease that still claims over 59,000 lives annually across more than 150 countries. The disease is nearly always fatal once symptoms appear. The global strategic plan prioritizes objectives defined in the theory of change, focusing on effective use of vaccines, medicines, tools, and technologies; reliable data for decision-making; sustained commitment to drive progress; and effective policies, governance, and support. Key objectives include expanding dog vaccination campaigns, improving awareness and education, and increasing access to healthcare and vaccines for at-risk populations. Sustained commitment and resources are critical to achieving these goals, with a focus on engaging stakeholders and demonstrating the impact of activities at national, regional, and global levels. Dog vaccination is a cornerstone of rabies prevention, as it stops transmission at its source. Vaccinating dogs is a cost-effective and sustainable way to save lives. The collaboration supports countries in conducting effective vaccination campaigns by providing access to affordable, safe, and effective vaccines through biological banks, strengthening veterinary services, and promoting innovative strategies to reach free-roaming dogs. Regional workshops and capacity-building initiatives further enhance national and regional networks, enabling countries to share knowledge and address local challenges. Timely and appropriate prophylaxis is nearly 100% effective, but access remains limited in many endemic areas. Expanding access to high-quality, affordable PEP relies on health systems capable of reaching underserved populations. The collaboration advocates for the inclusion of rabies PEP in global vaccine investment strategies and supports countries in forecasting vaccine needs, improving procurement practices, and integrating bite case management to reduce unnecessary costs. The collaboration also focuses on improving rabies diagnostics and surveillance to monitor progress, validate elimination, and target interventions. By refining tools and training technical staff, countries can enhance their surveillance systems and share data to inform decision-making. Integrated reporting systems for human and animal rabies data provide a comprehensive understanding of the disease burden and the impact of interventions. Advocacy plays a crucial role in engaging stakeholders and encouraging investment in rabies elimination. The collaboration develops advocacy materials and strategies to highlight the feasibility of elimination and promote prioritization within countries. Regional advocacy strategies focus on areas with the highest disease burden, involving local leaders and international champions to drive progress toward the Zero by 30 goal. In summary, the United Against Rabies collaboration provides a comprehensive framework for eliminating rabies through coordinated global efforts, country-led initiatives, and sustained commitment. By leveraging existing tools, building capacity, and fostering innovation, the collaboration aims to save lives, reduce costs, and achieve a world free from dog-mediated rabies by 2030.
